questions.question: Which CPU scheduling algorithm selects the process with the smallest next CPU burst?
questions.explanation: SJF always picks the ready process with the shortest next CPU burst, which minimises average waiting time.

questions.question: A situation in which two or more processes wait indefinitely for resources held by each other is called:
questions.explanation: In a deadlock every process in the set is waiting for a resource that another process in the set holds.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four necessary conditions for deadlock?
questions.explanation: Deadlock requires mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption and circular wait. Being able to preempt resources would break the no-preemption condition.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of virtual memory?

options.A: To make the CPU run faster
options.B: To let programs use more memory than is physically installed by using disk as an extension
options.C: To encrypt data stored in RAM
options.D: To increase the size of the CPU cache

questions.explanation: Virtual memory gives each process a large address space and keeps only the needed pages in RAM, swapping the rest to disk.

questions.question: Which page replacement algorithm replaces the page that has not been used for the longest period of time?
questions.explanation: LRU evicts the page whose last use is furthest in the past, assuming recent history predicts near-future use.
